children: By Summer Zhen

China's yuan dipped against the dollar on Thursday, as rising near-term Federal Reserve rate hike expectations drove the greenback higher, while cautious investors awaited the outcome of the Trump-Xi summit in Washington.

The US dollar rallied to its highest level in nearly two months overnight as investors' expectations of a near-term rate hike grew, pushing benchmark ​10-year Treasury yields to their highest since 2007.
Rising US yields and Fed tightening expectations have supported the dollar but heightened pressure on the yuan and other Asian currencies, analysts said.
The spot yuan
was 0.09% lower at 6.7171 to the dollar as of 0224 GMT, after trading in a range of 6.7141 to 6.7195.
Prior to the market opening, the People's Bank of China set the midpoint rate
at 6.7489 per dollar, 305 pips weaker than a Reuters estimate. The spot yuan is allowed to trade a maximum of 2% either side of the fixed midpoint each day.
US President Donald Trump welcomed Chinese President Xi Jinping to Washington on Wednesday for a three-day visit.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Fox News that Washington and Beijing agreed to extend their ‌trade truce through January 10. The two-month extension is shorter than markets expected.
With deep differences remaining on trade and technology, market participants maintain low expectations going into the talks, anticipating limited deliverables.
The offshore yuan traded at 6.7182 yuan per dollar
, down about 0.09% in Asian trade. The dollar's six-currency index
was at 101.15.

"The yuan's recent rally to a 3-1/2-year high reflects that markets have already partially priced in the stabilisations of US-China relations," Kaiyuan Securities said in a note. "Now the key focus is whether there are any new incremental developments regarding tariffs, technology, among other areas."

Separately, China's central bank said on Wednesday that it would ​inject up to 1 trillion yuan ($149 ‌billion) per day via short-term liquidity tools around the turn of the month as the ​Golden Week holiday nears.
OCBC strategists expect the yuan to keep familiar ranges as "upcoming China holidays could see liquidity thinned out."
